subject: Commercial fast-path: MAP, ramp commits & SLO-linked concessions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <mchen@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + commercial framing for quick path

Michael / Sarah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great discussion on the inference latency profile you need for the agent routing use case. Per our chat, attached is a one-page Mutual Action Plan (Acme_MAP_v1.pdf) and a short SLA appendix that outlines the latency SLO plumbing we can consider. High-level proposal for a "fast-path" close:

- 30-day evaluation with dedicated support and two configured endpoints that mirror your production traffic (prefix caching on request).
- Commercial: staged committed units with ramp milestones at 30/60/90 days.
- Discounts: 10% on first 6 months for the initial commit; additional 5% once 3x traffic ramp is reached.
- SLO trade: for a committed 99th p50/p99 latency target we can offer a 6-month rebate pool (up to 5% of committed spend) if we miss the p99 target more than 3x in a quarter.

Can you confirm the core commercial levers that matter to procurement (commit size, length, who signs)? If that looks directionally right I'll loop in our commercial lead for a short call to lock the numbers and timelines.

Next steps I propose:
- You review the MAP and SLA appendix (attached) and mark any must-haves.
- We schedule a 30-min commercial alignment (Ben + Marissa + your procurement lead).
- If green, we prepare a DocuSign with the commit schedule and an evaluation checklist.

Appreciate it — I want to keep this tight so you can hit your April budget window if possible.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
SLA_appendix_draft.docx (DOCX, 2 pages)
From: Michael Chen <mchen@acmecloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + commercial framing for quick path

Ben —

Thanks for the note and the draft MAP. A few quick clarifications from procurement and engineering:

- Our engineering team requires a baseline p99 <= 150ms for single-turn generation at our median prompt length; p50 needs to be ~40–60ms. We are open to a rebate model for misses but need a clear measurement method and SLA window.
- Commit size: we can commit to an initial 200k inference minutes/month for 6 months if pricing is competitive. Procurement will need a table of milestone discounts tied to concrete throughput targets.
- Ramp cadence: we prefer 30/60/120 to give our internal teams time for integration.

Also, legal wants obligation caps and a simple list of security deliverables before any private deployment. Can your team provide SOC2 evidence and an audit plan?

If you can map the discount bands to concrete monthly committed units, and specify the exact p99 measurement (time window, measurement agent, rolling window), we can push this through an expedited procurement review.

Can you set a call with your commercial lead and our procurement on Thursday?

Thanks,
Michael
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Cloud
mchen@acmecloud.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@acmecloud.com>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP draft + commercial framing for quick path — action items + proposed economics

Team — forwarding Acme's reply. Key asks: p99 <= 150ms, commit to 200k inference minutes/month for 6 months, and explicit milestone table (30/60/120). They prefer 30/60/120 rather than 30/60/90.

Proposed commercial structure (initial draft for internal review):
- Term: 6 months initial contract, auto-renew unless either party opts out with 30d notice.
- Commit: 200k/mins month 1, ramp to 600k/mins by month 4 (targets: 200k / 350k / 475k / 600k).
- Pricing: Base rate $0.018/min; initial commit discount 10% off base for months 1–3, additional 5% discount applied to months after they hit the 3x ramp (i.e., when monthly mins >= 600k).
- SLA concession: Target p99 <= 150ms as measured by our synthetic agent using customer-representative prompt set (we will run parallel measurements). If we miss p99 in any calendar month more than 3x (monthly windows), we put $X from a rebate pool (5% of that month's committed spend) into a credit that is applied to the next invoice.
- Measurement & audit: Redwood to provide daily latency dashboards + weekly export; customer can request an audit (data-sharing mutual NDA) for disputed windows.
- Security: Provide SOC2 Type II report and an evidence package; we can include a security carve-out in the MAP.

Ask from you all: 1) Marissa — can you confirm if this pricing aligns with quota/discount authority or if we need approval? 2) Rishi — can you confirm the rebate cap language and whether the 5% pool is acceptable from a commercial risk perspective? 3) Monica — legal to confirm basic SLA language and audit obligations; any must-have limitations for private deployment?

I'll set up a 30-min call with Acme (they asked for Thursday) — proposed slots: Thu 4/15 9:30am or 2:00pm PT.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@acmecloud.com>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP draft + commercial framing for quick path — action items + proposed economics

Thanks Ben — quick internal alignment after the call this morning. Notes and requested edits:

- Pricing authority: I can approve up to a 12% introductory discount without escalation. The extra 5% tied to ramp requires a quick approval from Ops Finance; I'll start that thread now.
- Rebate pool: 5% of committed monthly spend is reasonable but add a quarterly cap equal to 10% of total committed spend that quarter to limit downside.
- Measurement: agree to synthetic agent as primary measurement with both sides' instrumentation; add a clause that measurement disagreements escalate to a neutral third-party measurement (we'll propose a vendor if needed).
- Term: recommend adding a 90-day auto-rollback clause if performance issues persist after two consecutive rebate-triggering months (protects us from open-ended remediation).
- Legal items (Monica): we'll need a short SLA exhibit that includes uptime, latency measurement, and an exclusion list for force majeure/3rd-party infra events. Also propose adding SOC2 doc link in the MAP.

Next steps I will take today: pull the Ops Finance approval request for the ramp discount; Monica, can you draft a short SLA exhibit (based on the attached SLA_appendix_draft.docx) with the rebate cap and measurement escalation language? Rishi, if you can confirm the commercial risk tolerance on the proposed cap we can present a cleaned-up DocuSign by EOD Fri.

Michael/Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. We'll push a revised MAP + SLA exhibit into the Drive (link below) and follow up with DocuSign once internal approvals are done.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAcmeMAP
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567 (deal RDW-2027-ACME-42)

—Marissa
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
